transcript: Candidate Seven. Name the guard. Then name the move.
The sand's almost gone, Number Seven.
Time's up. You still haven't named it.
This is 'the rock that doesn't dig into you when you sit down'... Too long! Let's call it 'Comfy'!
It moved. During the exam... were you watching the guard the whole time?
That explains it. The ones on pages twelve and three are the same guard. I said that myself, back then.
Welcome aboard! I'll make your name tag later—
The one from the exam? It followed you out?
I'll help you remember the names later. You've already noticed its hands.
Sit down. Before we fight it, let's understand it.
Why are its hands longer now? Did the number change?
Don't name it. Look at its hands.
There's a blade in your pack: the arithmetic geometric mean inequality. It has three sockets. Fill all three before you strike.
You have two Focus points for this layer. Enough to check two things. Look first.
Look at what? Its two hands?
At its feet, it says X is greater than zero. Both hands are positive. The positive socket is filled.
Multiply them and you get twenty-five. That doesn't change with X. The constant socket is filled too.
One layer's off!
We still need equal. Can the two hands be the same length?
X equals five. That's within the allowed range. All three sockets are filled.
Did you see that? Both hands are the same length!
It's still there! It's about to hit back!
It's gone! It's gone! And you didn't use a single hint!
Two hands again? Why is this- why is this one wrapped in bandages?
The Registry Academy sent me to clear the wilds. Stand aside. Page three of the Register: the Product Guard.
Its name tells you which move to use. What are you staring at?
He's got the name right. He just doesn't know what's under the cloth.
I've been behind that rock, watching that cloth for a while now.
Don't send anyone in yet. First, look at what you can see on it.
The cloth's off. Underneath is X minus one, all in one piece.
One whole piece! Leave that to me. I'll bundle it up!
X and that piece... they're only one apart.
Both hands are positive. You can fill the positive socket on your equipment.
Now we can see it. Who will you send? Attach your reason to her.
I've seen this one before. Multiply one hand by the other, and you get a constant.
Next time something's missing... call me.
Next time! You have to pick me next time!
Its outer covering is broken. Before you strike, ask those three questions on the blade.
T equals three. That's within the allowed range. All three sockets are filled.
See that? Bundle it up! Snap!
It's still there... It's about to hit back.
Under the cloth, it's X minus one. But the other hand is X. Multiply those, and the product isn't constant.
Just luck. On the next page, I won't misread it again.
You were the one who saw through that cloth. I just stood beside you... and added the missing one.
Both hands are underground... Can yesterday's blade still cut it?
Pick me today! Fabia got to go yesterday. It's my turn now, isn't it?
If anything's missing today... I'm here.
One night later, it's standing differently. Do you still recognize it?
Two hands! Just like yesterday. Can we cut it straight away?
Their product is still nine. The hands are negative... but the product's positive.
The hands are negative. We can't use the blade. Who will you send? Attach your reason to her.
A different form, but the same problem. First, look at negative X, and negative nine divided by X.
They've flipped! They're positive now!
We still need the equal socket. After you strike, remember to flip it back.
X equals negative three. That's within the allowed range. All three sockets are filled.
Flip it, cut it, flip it back! Snap!
A day later, in a different form... and you still recognized it. This blade is yours now.
We've finally got a proper weapon in the pack! I'll give it a name— uh maybe-
It already has a name.
Then I'll give it another one!
Here's your compass. Which path shall we take first?
